blockers.description: Test 7 (live episode with depth recording): run_vla_episode.py connects to the Colab PolicyServer, sends policy instructions, model loads successfully (~30-40s), then the gRPC tunnel gives 'Connection refused' right as real inference is about to start. Reproduced identically 3x tonight: once on L4 GPU, twice on A100 GPU, across different Colab regions/VMs, different ngrok tunnel addresses. Root cause NOT confirmed -- the actual Python traceback is unrecoverable after the fact because Step 3's serve() call runs in a background thread (threading.Thread(target=serve, ...)), and Jupyter only captures stdout/stderr for whichever cell is synchronously executing at the time a background thread prints -- once that cell (in practice, whichever tunnel/depth cell happened to be running) finishes, later thread output is NOT captured into any saved cell output, so the real error is lost even after saving the notebook.
blockers.workaround: None yet applied. NEXT SESSION MUST FIRST modify Step 3's cell to redirect the serve() thread's stdout/stderr to a file (e.g. contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr to '/content/policy_server.log', or Python logging to a FileHandler) BEFORE attempting Test 7 again -- otherwise we will hit the exact same 'lost error' wall a 4th time. This is the single highest-priority action for the next session.

decisions.decision: Fixed 3 real bugs in policy_server.ipynb's FastFS depth pipeline: (1) scripts/run_demo.py's unconditional cv2.imshow/waitKey and Open3D viewer calls hang forever headless -- patched via sed in Step 7. (2) run_demo.py only writes depth_meter.npy when --get_pc 1, but Step 8's Flask handler passed --get_pc 0 -- fixed to --get_pc 1, and DEPTH_OUTPUT_GLOB narrowed from '*.npy' to the confirmed 'depth_meter.npy'.
decisions.rationale: Confirmed live during Test 6 UAT debugging -- discovered by systematically isolating FastFS's own bundled demo command from our wrapper.

decisions.decision: Test 6's accuracy check uses HSV red-color-threshold cube detection (project's own target is 'the red cube') sampling median depth over the detected region, instead of the originally-planned frame-center-pixel reading.
decisions.rationale: User correctly rejected the naive center-pixel approach as uninformative -- the depth model has no object semantics, so the center pixel could land on the robot arm, mat, or cube depending on framing. Cube-anchored detection ties the accuracy check to something concrete.

decisions.decision: Added GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native env var when invoking run_vla_episode.py.
decisions.rationale: grpc's bundled c-ares DNS resolver failed ('DNS query cancelled') on an ngrok TCP tunnel address that plain `dig`/`nc` proved was genuinely reachable -- a known class of macOS-specific grpc resolver bug, unrelated to tunnel health.

decisions.decision: Added a permanent `!pip uninstall -y torchaudio` cell to policy_server.ipynb right before Step 3.
decisions.rationale: lerobot's installs pull in a torchaudio build whose CUDA version doesn't reliably match Colab's preinstalled torch, crashing Step 3's serve() import 2x tonight with a cascading ModuleNotFoundError. torchaudio isn't used by anything in this notebook.

decisions.decision: Cleaned up policy_server.ipynb: removed ~15 live-debugging scratch cells (Xvfb setup, ad-hoc run_demo.py test invocations, sed/grep inspection commands) added during Test 6 diagnosis, folding the durable fixes into Steps 7/8 permanently.
decisions.rationale: Notebook is meant to be reusable across sessions; scratch diagnostic cells from one debugging session shouldn't accumulate permanently.

context_notes: Test 6 (depth accuracy) is a genuine, well-verified pass after a long debugging arc (3 real bugs fixed: headless-GUI hang, missing --get_pc flag, stale camera index). Test 7 has failed 3x tonight in a way that looks environmental at first (network blip theory, then 'too much load' theory, then 'parallel tunnels' theory) but none of those theories survived scrutiny against the actual evidence (same failure on L4 AND A100 with much more VRAM; depth tunnel stayed healthy while gRPC tunnel's backing process specifically died; ngrok's own logs showed clean tunnel opens both times). The user and I converged on: this is very likely a software bug inside the serve() background thread that crashes silently on the first real observation, and we currently have NO way to see the actual error because of how Jupyter captures (or fails to capture) background-thread output after its originating cell finishes. Also flagged and recovered from a real mistake this session: I ran `git checkout --` on policy_server.ipynb without checking git status first, discarding the user's live in-progress Colab edits from earlier in the session -- recovered via VS Code's local file history (~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/History/), verified content matched before restoring. No permanent damage, but worth remembering: always check git status/diff before any checkout/reset on a file being actively edited outside the git workflow (e.g. a notebook open in another editor).
